newsitem.title: CONGO: Fresh massacre of elephants in Congo.
newsitem.headline: Fresh massacre of elephants in Congo.

text.p: Ivory poachers have killed 30 elephants in northern Congo in an area where 200 elephants were slaughtered for their tusks in August, forestry officials said on Saturday.
The two massacres took place in the Saline de Muadie, an area where the animals go regularly in search of mineral salt, 1,000 km (600 miles) north of the capital Brazzaville.
Elephants are a protected species in Congo and trading in ivory is illegal.
Forestry officials estimate that many of Congo's more than 10,000 elephants are prey to poachers with only those in Odzala and Nouabale Ndoki national parks in the north properly protected.
The Saline de Muadie is near Odzala park. Forestry officials say they lack the staff to patrol the area effectively.
